# Command reference

Every command the binary accepts, in the order the CLI lists them.

```bash
python3 scripts/gen-cli-docs.py > docs/cli.md
```

## Usage

```
bs [OPTIONS] [PEER] [SESSION] [SUBCOMMANDS]
```

`PEER` alone attaches to (or starts) a session on that peer. `PEER` plus
`SESSION` reattaches to a named session. With no arguments on an interactive
terminal you get the fleet selector; with `--daemon` you get the relay daemon.

## Global options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-V,--version` | Display program version information and exit |
| `--config TEXT` | Config file path (default: ~/.bridgesessions/config) |
| `--config-dir TEXT` | Config directory (default: ~/.bridgesessions) |
| `--daemon` | Detach from terminal (daemonize) |
| `--cua-helper` | Run CUA helper server (screen capture + input injection in user session) |
| `-s,--select` | Interactively pick a session to attach (or start a new one) |
| `-l,--list` | List sessions on PEER (or local sessions when PEER is omitted) and exit |
| `-h,--help` | Print this help message and exit |

## Commands (31)

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| [`shell`](#shell) | Open an interactive shell (or run a command) on a peer. |
| [`connect`](#connect) | Interactive two-step selector: pick a fleet peer, then pick a launch harness (a command the peer runs to start a session, e.g. |
| [`sessions`](#sessions) | List sessions on this node (omit PEER) or on a remote PEER. |
| [`keygen`](#keygen) | Generate this node's ed25519 identity keypair. |
| [`authorize`](#authorize) | Authorize a peer's ed25519 public key for direct connections. |
| [`doctor`](#doctor) | Check local configuration: identity keys, config parse, daemon reachability, listen port, and app-home layout. |
| [`rotate-identity`](#rotate-identity) | Regenerate this node's identity keys (peers must re-pin the new pubkey). |
| [`peers`](#peers) | Manage seed peers: list, add, remove. |
| [`health`](#health) | Ping/pong health check against a peer: verifies TLS handshake, identity pins, and the data plane. |
| [`reconnect`](#reconnect) | Ask the local daemon to tear down and re-handshake one peer (fresh TLS + gossip). |
| [`invite`](#invite) | Generate a single-use invite token a new node can `bs join` with. |
| [`enroll`](#enroll) | Vouch for a new mesh member: sign its node entry and gossip the key to all peers, so the member is trusted mesh-wide without per-peer `authorize` calls. |
| [`join`](#join) | Join an existing mesh using an invite token from a member. |
| [`image`](#image) | Render an image file inline in the terminal (Sixel/Block art, depending on terminal support). |
| [`anim`](#anim) | Play an animated GIF inline in the terminal (frame-by-frame rendering; Ctrl-C stops). |
| [`stats`](#stats) | Show local daemon statistics: connections, sessions, transfer totals, and per-peer counters. |
| [`fleet`](#fleet) | Show the live fleet directory gathered by the daemon: every known peer with address, version, health status, and resource usage (cpu/mem/disk where reported). |
| [`upgrade`](#upgrade) | Self-update this node's binary from GitHub releases (or another node with --all). |
| [`telemetry`](#telemetry) | Show transfer telemetry: file-transfer and stream byte counters per peer. |
| [`file`](#file) | File transfer between peers over the mesh (mTLS, chunked). |
| [`capture-video`](#capture-video) | Record the peer's screen to a video (via its CUA helper), transfer it back with file recv, and print the local path. |
| [`cua`](#cua) | Computer-use automation on a remote peer: screen size, screenshots, and synthetic mouse/keyboard input. |
| [`vfolder`](#vfolder) | Virtual folder sync: keep a local directory mirrored to a peer path (push, pull, or bidirectional) on an interval. |
| [`sync`](#sync) | Cross-machine folder mirroring (bs sync pair …). |
| [`edit`](#edit) | Edit a remote file locally: copies PEER:PATH to a temp file, opens $EDITOR, and writes it back on save. |
| [`run-script`](#run-script) | Send a local script to a peer and execute it there. |
| [`job`](#job) | Multi-step JSON jobs: run an ordered list of commands on a peer with per-step results (more robust than long && chains). |
| [`script`](#script) | Content-addressed script cache: store scripts once (hash-named), then push/run them on peers by name or hash. |
| [`pane`](#pane) | Publish content to the BridgePanel surface (web dashboard) of a session on this node. |
| [`api`](#api) | Query the daemon JSON API (sessions\|peers\|daemon\|events [since_id]). |
| [`run`](#run) | Launch a command as a persistent background service (daemon-supervised) Run `bs <command> --help` for detailed help on any command. |

### shell

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-n,--name TEXT` | Session name |
| `-s,--select` | Interactively pick a session to attach |
| `-x,--cmd TEXT` | Command override |
| `--cols UINT` | Terminal columns |
| `--rows UINT` | Terminal rows |
| `-r,--record` | Record session output to file Forward Ctrl-C to remote child (default: on) Send HUP/TERM/INT/QUIT/KILL to the child when the last peer detaches (default: none) |
| `--detach` | Send command and return immediately (session runs on peer) |
| `--wait` | Block until the named session exits, then return its exit code |
| `-i,--interactive` | Run the -x command as a full interactive terminal session (raw mode, no ANSI stripping) — required for TUI apps like hermes --tui Examples: bs shell dev Interactive shell on peer 'dev' bs shell dev -n build Named session (reattach later) bs shell dev -x 'docker ps' Run a one-shot command bs shell dev -x htop -i Interactive TUI command (raw mode) bs shell dev -x ./long-job --detach Fire-and-forget; runs on peer bs shell dev -n build --wait Block until session exits |

### peers

| Option | Description |
|---|---|

**`peers list`** — List configured peers with address, pubkey pin, and last status.

**`peers add`** — Add a seed peer (address + optional pinned pubkey). The pubkey is required when mesh.require_seed_pins=true (recommended).

**`peers remove`** — Remove a seed peer from the config.

**`peers rotate-pin`** — Update a peer's pinned pubkey (after the peer rotated its identity)

### file

| Option | Description |
|---|---|

**`file send`** — Send a file to a peer. Lands under the peer's receive_dir unless an explicit remote dest is given (home/tmp dest requires the peer's file.dest_allow_home). Use --wait to block until the peer acknowledges completion.

**`file recv`** — Receive a file from a peer (run on the target node). Pulls the remote path into a local directory; --wait blocks until the transfer completes or fails.

### capture-video

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--fps INT` | Frames per second (default 2) |
| `--duration INT` | Duration in seconds (default 15) |
| `--quality INT` | Quality 1-100 (default 70) |
| `--max-width INT` | Max width, 0=native (default 1280) Example: bs capture-video dev --duration 30 --fps 4 |

### cua

| Option | Description |
|---|---|

**`cua screen`** — Get remote screen dimensions (width x height).

**`cua capture`** — Capture a screenshot from the peer (PNG default; --output writes a file instead of stdout).

**`cua click`** — Click the mouse at coordinates (--button left|right|middle).

**`cua move`** — Move the mouse to coordinates.

**`cua type`** — Type text into the peer's focused window.

**`cua key`** — Press a HID key code (e.g. 40=Enter, 44=Q; see USB HID usage ids).

**`cua scroll`** — Scroll the mouse wheel (--direction up|down, --amount ticks).

| Option | Description |

**`vfolder add`** — Add a mapping. --dir push|pull|bidirectional; --interval seconds.

**`vfolder sync`** — Trigger an immediate sync of one mapping.

**`vfolder list`** — List active folder mappings.

### job

| Option | Description |
|---|---|

**`job run`** — Execute a job JSON file on a peer. --stop-on-error aborts remaining steps after the first failure (default: run all steps).

### script

| Option | Description |
|---|---|

**`script add`** — Add a script file to the local cache (optionally with an alias).

**`script list`** — List cached scripts (name, hash, size).

**`script push`** — Push a cached script to a peer's cache.

**`script run`** — Run a cached script on a peer; extra args after -- pass to it.

**`script remove`** — Remove a script from the local cache.

### run

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--self` | Target this node (the local daemon) |
| `--peer TEXT` | Remote peer (not supported yet) |
| `--name TEXT` | Service name |
| `--status` | Show service status (filter with --name) |
| `--stop TEXT` | Stop the named service (kills its process group) |
| `--logs TEXT` | Tail the named service's log Examples: bs run --self --name worker -- ./agent.sh Start a supervised service bs run --self --status List run services bs run --self --status --name worker One service bs run --self --stop worker Kill + stop supervision bs run --self --logs worker Tail the service log The daemon restarts the command with capped backoff (max 60s) if it fails. |
